hypothesis: Providing boards with a standardized, minimal AI oversight toolkit (dashboards, inventories, reporting and policy templates, and challenge guides) that is auto-generated from the same underlying AI risk data will improve (a) completeness and consistency of board AI risk coverage and (b) usability for non-technical directors, relative to current ad-hoc, manually assembled packs.

baseline.description: Current-state, manually prepared AI oversight materials used for board and risk committee meetings, assembled without the unified Chapter 14 toolkit or auto-generation pipeline.
artifacts: Manual slide deck describing key AI initiatives and risks (e.g., PowerPoint/PDF) created by risk/AI teams for board or risk committee.
Unstructured AI model list or spreadsheet (if available) without standardized risk inventory fields (e.g., no consistent criticality, autonomy level, or systemic impact ratings).
Generic risk heatmap that mixes AI and non-AI risks without explicit linkage to AI systems or systemic risk pathways.
Narrative-only board paper for AI incidents or near-misses (free-text documents without a common schema).
Existing AI or model risk policies not harmonized into an explicit, board-level AI use policy and AI risk appetite statement.
data_source_requirements: At least one recent (≤ 12 months) board or risk committee pack that includes AI-related content.
Existing model inventory, product inventory, or risk register that flags AI/ML use-cases (even if incomplete).
At least one documented AI incident or near-miss, or a proxy incident in model risk, operational risk, or conduct risk attributed to algorithmic behavior.

treatment.description: Use of a unified, reproducible Chapter 14 toolkit implementation that ingests the same AI risk data and generates a standardized board pack: AI risk inventory, heatmaps, board-level dashboards, policy and escalation templates, challenge guides, and incident/near-miss templates.

components.name: Minimal Viable AI Oversight Pack Generator
components.description: Script or notebook that reads standardized AI inventory and incident data and automatically produces a board-ready pack (e.g., static HTML/PDF or slide export) including key exhibits from sections 14.2–14.6.

components.name: AI Risk Inventory Template and Heatmap Engine
components.description: Data schema and notebook/web app that captures AI systems with standardized fields (criticality, autonomy, systemic impact channels, third-party dependence, controls in place) and generates portfolio-level heatmaps.

components.name: Board-Level AI Risk Dashboard
components.description: Simple dashboard (e.g., Streamlit/Plotly/BI-like) showing a small, opinionated set of board-level indicators: number of high-criticality AI systems, open validation issues, incidents by severity, key metrics from Chapter 6, mapped to business lines.

components.name: Policy and Escalation Template Library
components.description: Version-controlled, parameterizable text templates for AI Use Policy, AI Risk Appetite Statement, and AI Escalation Protocols, designed to be instantiated for the institution via configuration (e.g., YAML/JSON).

components.name: Challenge Guides and Question Packs
components.description: Structured, machine-readable lists of board questions organized by committee and topic (e.g., credit AI, trading AI, fraud AI), with simple filters and export to PDF/Word/Markdown.

components.name: AI Incident and Near-Miss Reporting Forms
components.description: Schema and form generator for standardized AI incident/near-miss reporting, including fields for systemic pathways, model behavior, business impact, and controls; output compatible with the dashboard and board pack.

components.name: Customization Profiles
components.description: Configuration-driven variants of the toolkit for at least three archetypes (universal bank, digital bank/fintech, asset manager/insurer) and at least two regulatory geographies (e.g., EU, US/UK) altering labels, metrics emphasis, and policy language blocks.

treatment_principles: Baseline and treatment must use the same underlying AI inventory and incident dataset so that differences in results are due to the toolkit, not the underlying risk data.
Treatment must be executable end-to-end by a technical practitioner using repository code, producing artifacts in standard formats (HTML, PDF, CSV, Markdown).
Toolkit defaults should align with the book’s governance framing and financial-services-specific systemic risk emphasis.

workloads.name: W1-universal-bank-quarterly-pack
workloads.description: Apply both baseline and treatment approaches to create AI oversight materials for a universal bank’s quarterly risk committee meeting.

inputs.institution_profile: Large universal bank operating in EU and US, with AI in credit underwriting, trading signal generation, fraud detection, and customer service.

data.ai_inventory: CSV/JSON of ~30 AI/ML systems with fields: system_id, business_line, product, AI_type, autonomy_level, criticality_tier, financial_exposure, systemic_pathways, vendor_flag, geography, validation_status.
data.incidents: AI incident/near-miss log for last 12–24 months with severity, business_impact, root_cause, remediation_status.
data.existing_policies: Text/PDF of current AI/model risk policies and risk appetite statements.
data.board_calendar: High-level board and risk committee calendar with standing agenda items.

baseline: Use existing processes to prepare the next board/risk committee pack that includes AI-related risks, drawing only on existing templates and practices.
Record preparation time, number of contributors, and pages/slides related to AI oversight.
Have 5–10 eligible senior stakeholders (directors, executives, or equivalent) independently score the pack using a standardized rubric (see metrics).
treatment: Normalize the same AI inventory and incident data to the repository’s schema.
Run the AI Risk Inventory Template and Heatmap Engine to produce AI portfolio views.

Run the Board-Level AI Risk Dashboard and Oversight Pack Generator to create a standardized board pack with integrated heatmaps, dashboard snapshots, incident summaries, and tailored challenge questions.
Instantiate draft AI Use Policy, AI Risk Appetite, and Escalation Protocol templates using configuration appropriate to the bank’s profile.
Share the treatment pack with a *different but comparable* group of 5–10 senior stakeholders (or the same group after a sufficient washout period) to score using the same rubric.

workloads.name: W2-digital-bank-monthly-ops-review
workloads.description: Test toolkit usability and coverage for a smaller, more automated digital bank during a monthly executive ops and risk review.

inputs.institution_profile: Digital bank/fintech heavily reliant on AI for onboarding, KYC, fraud, and personalization; operating primarily in one jurisdiction.

data.ai_inventory: Smaller set (~10–15) of AI systems with comparatively high autonomy and operational criticality.
data.incidents: Operational incident log including AI-related false positives/negatives in fraud and onboarding.
data.governance: Simpler committee structure and limited formal AI policy texts.

baseline: Use current methods (often ad-hoc) to brief executives on AI risks during a monthly ops review.
Record preparation effort and capture participant feedback on clarity and coverage.
treatment: Apply the same toolkit pipeline to generate a right-sized AI oversight pack configured for a digital bank archetype.
Collect analogous feedback and preparation metrics.

workloads.name: W3-asset-manager-annual-board-strategy
workloads.description: Assess the toolkit’s adaptability to an asset manager or insurer during an annual strategy and risk deep-dive focused on AI in investment and pricing models.

inputs.institution_profile: Asset manager or insurer using AI in portfolio construction, risk analytics, and pricing/underwriting.

data.ai_inventory: ~10–20 AI models tied to portfolios or product lines, tagged with assets under management or premium volume influenced by each model.
data.incidents: Log of model risk events and near-misses (e.g., mispricing, model drift, limit breaches) with AI attribution.
data.regulatory_context: Region-specific conduct, suitability, solvency and product governance requirements.

baseline: Prepare the existing annual AI risk and model risk update for the board using current documents and slides only.
Capture the structure and perceived completeness of systemic risk coverage.
treatment: Configure the toolkit for an asset manager/insurer profile and relevant geography.
Generate AI risk inventory, heatmaps, dashboard views, and tailored challenge questions emphasizing conduct, liquidity/systemic spillovers, and capital/solvency angle.
Collect comparable feedback and effort metrics.

data_controls: Use exactly the same AI inventory and incident dataset for both baseline and treatment in each workload.
Freeze datasets before experiment execution and store them version-controlled in the repository (or referenced via checksums) to ensure reproducibility.
Redact all personally identifiable information and confidential details; use synthetic or anonymized data where necessary.
participant_controls: Use comparable participant profiles (e.g., directors, C-suite, senior risk leaders) for baseline and treatment assessments within each workload.
If re-using the same participants, enforce a washout period and counterbalance the order (some see baseline first, others see treatment first) to reduce order bias.
Ensure participants are blinded to which materials are baseline vs toolkit-generated when scoring packs.
process_controls: Time-box preparation windows and record actual preparation hours for baseline and treatment separately.
Standardize the evaluation rubric and survey instruments across workloads.
Ensure that the toolkit configuration is documented and kept constant for all treatment runs within a workload.
technical_controls: Pin code dependencies (requirements.txt, lockfile, or environment.yml) and document exact versions.
Run all treatment scripts in a clean environment using the provided run instructions.
Log run configuration, timestamps, and commit hashes associated with each generated artifact.

metrics.name: prep_time_hours
metrics.description: Total human time spent preparing the AI-related portion of the board/committee materials for a given meeting.

metrics.name: num_artifacts
metrics.description: Number of distinct AI oversight artifacts presented (e.g., inventory tables, heatmaps, dashboards, incident summaries, policy summaries, question lists).

metrics.name: coverage_score
metrics.description: Average expert/board rating of how completely the materials cover AI systemic risk dimensions: inventory visibility, criticality, systemic pathways, incidents, controls, and open issues.

metrics.name: clarity_score
metrics.description: Average rating by directors/executives of how understandable the AI oversight materials are to a non-technical audience.

metrics.name: actionability_score
metrics.description: Average rating of how well the pack supports concrete board actions (e.g., decisions, challenges, follow-ups).

metrics.name: customization_effort
metrics.description: Incremental time required to adapt the toolkit outputs (treatment) to a specific business model and geography beyond base generation (e.g., editing policy templates, labels, committee names).

metrics.name: consistency_score
metrics.description: Expert assessment of internal consistency between artifacts in the same pack (e.g., heatmap cells align with inventory, incidents align with dashboard metrics).

metrics.name: incident_structuring_score
metrics.description: Expert assessment of how well incident/near-miss reporting templates capture key attributes relevant to systemic risk, root cause analysis, and governance escalation.

metrics.name: question_coverage_score
metrics.description: Board/audience assessment of whether provided challenge guides and question lists meaningfully support oversight and challenge across key AI risk areas.

primary: For each workload, treatment reduces prep_time_hours for AI oversight materials by at least 20% relative to baseline, after an initial learning period, without reducing coverage_score or clarity_score.
Across all workloads, treatment improves average coverage_score and clarity_score by ≥ 0.5 points (on a 1–5 scale) versus baseline.
Consistency_score for treatment packs is ≥ 4.0 on average and at least 0.5 points higher than the corresponding baseline scores.
secondary: Actionability_score and question_coverage_score under treatment are ≥ 4.0 on average across workloads.
Customization_effort for adapting the toolkit to a new institution profile within the same archetype (e.g., another universal bank) is ≤ 4 person-hours.
Incident_structuring_score for the treatment’s incident templates is ≥ 4.0 and at least 0.5 points above baseline incident documentation practices.
interpretation_notes: Failure to meet all thresholds does not invalidate the toolkit but indicates where further iteration is needed (e.g., usability vs coverage trade-offs).
Qualitative feedback from participants should be logged and used to contextualize metric movements, especially in smaller institutions where N is limited.

failure_modes.name: data_misalignment
failure_modes.description: AI inventory and incident data are incomplete or inconsistent across baseline and treatment runs, confounding comparisons.
mitigations: Run a data quality check script before both baseline and treatment.
Impute or clearly mark missing fields; avoid using records with critical missingness in analysis.
Document any manual data cleaning steps.

failure_modes.name: participant_bias
failure_modes.description: Participants know which pack is toolkit-generated and unconsciously favor or disfavor it; or treatment is always reviewed second, benefiting from learning effects.
mitigations: Blind participants to condition labels; present both as alternative formats A and B.
Randomize order of exposure where feasible.
Use the same evaluation rubric across conditions and workloads.

failure_modes.name: scope_creep_in_treatment
failure_modes.description: Practitioners add extra custom analysis or manual curation to the treatment pack but not to the baseline, overstating the toolkit’s benefits.
mitigations: Clearly distinguish between auto-generated content and additional manual additions.
Track manual customization time separately (contributing to customization_effort).
Limit manual edits to content that could reasonably be parameterized in future iterations.

failure_modes.name: overfitting_to_example_institution
failure_modes.description: Toolkit design and defaults are tuned excessively to one archetype (e.g., universal bank in EU), reducing generalizability.
mitigations: Ensure at least three archetype-specific profiles (universal bank, digital bank, asset manager/insurer) are exercised.
Document configuration differences across profiles in the repository.
Collect and compare metrics across workloads to identify profile-specific weaknesses.

failure_modes.name: technical_environment_issues
failure_modes.description: Differences in software versions, libraries, or OS environments cause divergent outputs or failures to run the toolkit.
mitigations: Provide a containerized environment (e.g., Docker) or reproducible environment specification.
Pin dependencies and run automated smoke tests before experimentation.
Log environment metadata in experiment outputs.

failure_modes.name: misinterpretation_of_metrics
failure_modes.description: Executives interpret coverage_score or clarity_score differently across conditions or workloads, lowering reliability.
mitigations: Provide clear, written definitions and examples for each rubric dimension.
Run a brief calibration exercise with participants before collecting scores.
Where possible, include multiple raters and analyze inter-rater agreement.

software: Python 3.10+ (or as specified in repository environment file).
Visualization/dashboard libraries: plotly and/or matplotlib, plus a simple web framework like Streamlit or Dash, or notebook environment (e.g., Jupyter).
PDF/HTML/Markdown export tools (e.g., nbconvert, weasyprint, or equivalent).
YAML/JSON parser for configuration-driven customization (e.g., PyYAML).
Optional: container runtime (Docker/Podman) if using provided images.
hardware: Standard modern laptop or VM with at least 8 GB RAM and several GB free disk space.
No GPU required; compute requirements are modest as workloads are metadata- and visualization-heavy, not model-training-heavy.
access: Local or secure network access to the anonymized/synthetic AI inventory and incident datasets.
Read/write access to the experiment’s output directory within a secure project workspace.
For real institutional deployments, appropriate data governance approvals and redaction processes must be in place.

run_instructions: Clone the repository https://github.com/bookauthority/boardroom-blind-spots and checkout the tag or branch corresponding to this experiment specification (e.g., `git checkout exp-ch14-boardroom-toolkits-v1`).

Set up the environment using the provided instructions (e.g., `conda env create -f environment.yml` or `pip install -r requirements.txt`). Optionally, build and run the provided container image if available.

Prepare input datasets for each workload: W1 (universal bank), W2 (digital bank), W3 (asset manager/insurer). Use the documented schemas in the `data_schemas/` directory. Place cleaned and versioned datasets under `data/inputs/<workload_id>/`.

Run the baseline preparation documentation script (if provided) or record manual baseline preparation processes for each workload. Store any baseline packs under `outputs/baseline/<workload_id>/` and log preparation_time and participants in a metadata file (see evidence_schema).

Execute the AI Risk Inventory and Heatmap Engine for each workload: `python tools/inventory_heatmap.py --config configs/<workload_id>.yml --input data/inputs/<workload_id>/ai_inventory.csv --output outputs/treatment/<workload_id>/inventory_heatmap/`.

Execute the Board-Level Dashboard generator: either run `streamlit run dashboards/board_ai_dashboard.py -- --config configs/<workload_id>.yml` to view interactively, or run a headless export script (e.g., `python dashboards/export_board_views.py`) to generate static artifacts (PNG/HTML) under `outputs/treatment/<workload_id>/dashboard_views/`.
Instantiate policy and escalation templates using configuration files: `python tools/generate_policies.py --config configs/<workload_id>.yml --output outputs/treatment/<workload_id>/policies/`.

Generate AI incident and near-miss reports from the incidents dataset: `python tools/incident_reporter.py --config configs/<workload_id>.yml --input data/inputs/<workload_id>/incidents.csv --output outputs/treatment/<workload_id>/incidents/`.
Generate challenge guides and question lists for relevant committees: `python tools/question_packs.py --config configs/<workload_id>.yml --output outputs/treatment/<workload_id>/questions/`.

Run the Minimal Viable AI Oversight Pack Generator to combine inventory views, heatmaps, dashboard snapshots, incident summaries, policy snippets, and challenge guides into a single pack: `python tools/generate_board_pack.py --config configs/<workload_id>.yml --sources outputs/treatment/<workload_id>/ --output outputs/treatment/<workload_id>/board_pack/`.

For each workload, organize blinded evaluation sessions where participants review baseline and treatment materials (labeled generically) and complete the standardized evaluation survey. Store raw survey data under `data/evaluations/<workload_id>/` with appropriate anonymization.

Compute experiment metrics by running the analysis script: `python analysis/evaluate_toolkit_effects.py --inputs data/evaluations/ --metadata data/metadata/ --outputs outputs/analysis/`. This script should read baseline and treatment metadata, compute metrics defined in this specification, and output structured evidence conforming to evidence_schema.
Document any deviations from these instructions, environment differences, or data issues in a run log file (e.g., `outputs/run_logs/<timestamp>.md`) for reproducibility and later interpretation.

evidence_schema.description: Schema for logging experimental runs and results without asserting outcomes in advance.

repository_commit.description: Git commit hash used for the run.

evaluation_scores.description: Per-participant scores for clarity, coverage, actionability, consistency, incident structuring, and question coverage.

analysis.description: Optional, computed comparison metrics between baseline and treatment for each workload.

notes.description: Free-text field capturing deviations from protocol, data issues, or contextual information needed for interpretation.
